quote: We experiment with two graph generation tasks, primarily focusing on ExplaGraphs ... and also experiment with another related task of temporal graph generation.

“T5 have led to significant advances in many natural language generation tasks like text summarization and machine translation… We study PLMs that generate explanation graphs in an end‑to‑end manner… tasks of explanation graph generation and temporal graph generation.”
Pre-trained sequence-to-sequence language models (PLMs) like BART and T5 have led to significant advances in many natural language generation tasks like text summarization and machine translation.
outputs: explanation graphs (linearized edge strings representing structured knowledge)
The models generate structured outputs in the form of explanation graphs and temporal graphs, represented as linearized strings of edges.

quote: we report StCA and SeCA along with other metrics like Graph-BertScore (G-BS) ... Graph Edit Distance (GED) and Edge Accuracy (EA).

“We evaluate explanation graphs by defining two accuracy metrics – (1) Structural Correctness Accuracy (StCA) … (2) Semantic Correctness Accuracy (SeCA) … We also report Graph‑BertScore (G‑BS), Graph Edit Distance (GED) and Edge Accuracy (EA).”
We vary the amount of training data from 500 to 2368 samples (all) and report StCA and SeCA along with other metrics like Graph-BertScore (G-BS) introduced in prior work.

“SeCA is a model‑based metric that computes the fraction of graphs that are both structurally and semantically correct. For computing SeCA, prior work trains a 3‑way RoBERTa classifier that given a belief and a generated explanation graph, infers whether the graph supports the belief, counters the belief or is incorrect.”

We conduct human evaluation to further validate our findings. We compare the graphs generated by T5 and our Max-Margin model on Amazon Mechanical Turk where three annotators choose which graph is better or if they are mostly similar (instructions in Appendix F).
guideline: Annotators choose which graph is better or if they are mostly similar.
Annotators are asked to select which of two graphs is better or indicate that they are mostly similar.

Annotators were instructed to compare two graphs and choose which one is better or if they are mostly similar, focusing on cases where both models predict the correct stance and the graphs are structurally correct to isolate semantic quality.
